It implements a client/server/daemon architecture"}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.li><_components.strong>{"adb client"}</_components.strong>{": invoked by you on the host machine (e.g., "}<_components.code>{"adb pull"}</_components.code>{")."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li><_components.strong>{"adb server"}</_components.strong>{": a background process on the host that manages connections."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li><_components.strong>{"adbd (daemon)"}</_components.strong>{": runs on the Android device and handles commands from the host."}</_components.li>{"\n"}</_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Connections usually go over USB, but "}<_components.code>{"adb"}</_components.code>{" can also operate over TCP (adb tcpip), which has additional risks. the program still waits for "}<_components.code>{"adb"}</_components.code>{" to exit."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"Return "}<_components.code>{"true"}</_components.code>{"/"}<_components.code>{"false"}</_components.code>{" depending on process exit status and write a timestamped entry to the local log."}</_components.li>{"\n"}</_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Why parse "}<_components.code>{"adb"}</_components.code>{" stderr?"}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.li><_components.code>{"adb pull"}</_components.code>{" prints transfer progress to "}<_components.code>{"stderr"}</_components.code>{" (on many devices) rather than "}<_components.code>{"stdout"}</_components.code>{". Parsing that gives a smooth per-file progress experience."}</_components.li>{"\n"}</_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Caveat: "}<_components.code>{"adb"}</_components.code>{" output is not standardized across all Android versions or vendor implementations. The current implementation covers the common case (percent values)."}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.hr />{"\n"}<_components.h1>{"The interactive flow (what the user spaces"}</_components.h3>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"We call "}<_components.code>{"Command::new(\"adb\").args([...])"}</_components.code>{", passing the remote path as one argument. The OS-level argument handling ensures spaces are preserved — no shell quoting required."}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.h3>{"Directories & recursive pulls"}</_components.h3>{"\n"}<_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.li><_components.code>{"adb pull"}</_components.code>{" supports pulling a directory recursively (e.g., "}<_components.code>{"adb pull /sdcard/DCIM ~/DCIM"}</_components.code>{")."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"When marking a directory, the CLI will call "}<_components.code>{"adb pull"}</_components.code>{" with the directory path; "}<_components.code>{"adb"}</_components.code>{" will pull its contents recursively."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"Be mindful of large directories: the progress parser will typically report per-file progress rather than full-directory bytes."}</_components.li>{"\n"}</_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.h3>{"Permissions & protected dirs"}</_components.h3>{"\n"}<_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"Non-rooted devices deny reads to "}<_components.code>{"/data"}</_components.code>{" and other protected directories."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"If you need protected content you must root the device or use adbd with appropriate privileges — not recommended except in controlled developer contexts."}</_components.li>{"\n"}</_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.hr />{"\n"}<_components.h1>{"Security considerations"}</_components.h1>{"\n"}<_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.li><_components.strong>{"USB Debugging risks"}</_components.strong>{": Keep USB debugging off when not actively using it.
